about: Paramount Syntex manufactures recycled acrylic fibre and a range of yarns (acrylic, polyester, nylon, wool and blended) at its integrated plant in Ludhiana, Punjab, with in-house fibre processing, tow and hank dyeing and spinning. It converts imported and domestic waste acrylic fibre into value-added products for apparel, hosiery and home textiles. FY26 revenue was about Rs 122 crore with 88.8% average capacity utilisation.
sector: Textiles - Synthetic Yarn and Recycled Fibre
headquarters: Mumbai, Maharashtra (registered office); factory at Ludhiana, Punjab

objects.purpose: Purchase of machinery at existing facilities (capex)
General corporate purposes (capped at lower of 15% of gross proceeds or Rs 10 crore)

promoters.background: Promoters Punit Arora (Managing Director, 88.51% pre-issue) and Kumkum Arora (Whole Time Director, 3.23%) bring over 30 years of combined textile industry experience.

concentration.note: Top 10 customers were 54.81% of FY26 sales (54.93% FY25, 67.36% FY24); top 10 suppliers were 62.61% of FY26 raw material purchases. No long-term agreements.

litigation_note: Against the company: 9 statutory/regulatory and 20 taxation matters, amount disclosed Rs 5.29 crore; company has filed 1 case of Rs 1.98 crore. One case by promoters/directors of Rs 20 crore. 15 matters against group entities involving Rs 50.67 crore. Contingent liabilities Rs 1.31 crore at Mar-26.
strengths: Integrated plant with in-house fibre processing, tow dyeing, hank dyeing and spinning gives control over quality and cost.
Recycles waste acrylic fibre into yarn, a sustainability-linked model with lower raw material cost.
Profitability improved sharply: PAT Rs 13.87 crore in FY26 versus Rs 1.35 crore in FY24, with 11.36% PAT margin.
Capacity utilisation rose from 76.97% to 88.77% over FY24-FY26, supporting the expansion case.
Debt to equity fell from 2.32 to 0.78 and ROCE rose to 29.18% in FY26.
Promoters have over 30 years of combined textile experience and hold 91.74% pre-issue.
Diverse product range across acrylic, polyester, nylon, wool and blended yarns plus fibre and job work.
ISO 9001, 14001 and 45001 certified with in-house quality control and R&D.

risks.title: Customer and supplier concentration
risks.detail: Top 10 customers were 54.81% of FY26 sales and top 10 suppliers 62.61% of raw material purchases, with no long-term agreements.

risks.title: Negative operating cash flow history
risks.detail: Operating cash flow was negative Rs 0.74 crore in FY24 and negative Rs 2.57 crore in FY25, turning positive Rs 5.90 crore only in FY26.

risks.title: High borrowings and thin cash
risks.detail: Borrowings of Rs 33.25 crore against net worth of Rs 42.67 crore, nearly all short-term (Rs 27.70 crore), while cash is only Rs 0.31 crore.

risks.title: Capex plan not appraised and orders not placed
risks.detail: Rs 61.68 crore machinery spend is not appraised by any bank, and orders for 100% of the machinery are yet to be placed, risking delay and cost overrun.

risks.title: Outstanding litigation
risks.detail: 29 cases against the company (9 statutory, 20 tax; Rs 5.29 crore), a Rs 20 crore case by promoters and Rs 50.67 crore of matters against group entities.

risks.title: Extensive related-party dealings
risks.detail: Loans, rent, purchases and sales with directors, group companies and firms under common management, with outstanding advances and trade balances in FY26.

risks.title: Statutory compliance lapses
risks.detail: Delays in GST, EPF, ESIC and TDS filings led to penalties and interest; GST and income tax demands of Rs 1.31 crore are contingent liabilities.

risks.title: Imported raw material and missing early records
risks.detail: Waste fibre is imported from Thailand and China, exposing the firm to supply and currency risk; historical records from 1996-2006 are unavailable and assumptions were used.

notes: Restated standalone Indian GAAP figures, converted from Rs lakh to Rs crore. Financial statement tables were garbled; values reconstructed and cross-checked against KPI tables (net worth, EBITDA, PAT margin, debt/equity). EBITDA as reported by company (PBT + depreciation + interest - other income). Cash is cash and cash equivalents only. Price band, issue size, P/E and post-issue promoter holding are blank in the RHP. Pre/post-issue shares assume full allotment of 64,40,000 fresh shares (includes 3,23,000 market maker portion). NAV per share is after the 30:1 bonus. Litigation counts as printed; case-count to amount mapping in the RHP table is slightly ambiguous.
